summary: Abraham's servant prayed for God to show him the right wife for Isaac. Rebekah kindly offered to water his camels, just as he had prayed, and she agreed to go.

story_reel.narration: Abraham was very old, and he wanted to find a wife for Isaac from his own family back home. So he sent his most trusted servant on a long journey with ten camels. When the servant reached a well outside the city, he stopped and prayed: 'Yahweh, God of my master Abraham, please give me success today. When the young women come to get water, let the one who says, Have a drink, and I'll water your camels too, be the one You've chosen for Isaac.' Before he even finished praying, a young woman named Rebekah came out with a water jar. The servant asked for a drink. Rebekah said, 'Drink, my lord!' Then she said, 'I'll get water for your camels too!' Ten thirsty camels drink a lot of water, but Rebekah kept running back and forth until they were all finished. The servant bowed and worshiped. He said, 'Yahweh has led me on the way!' When Rebekah's family asked her, 'Will you go?' she said, 'I will go.' And Isaac loved her.

memory_verse.text: As for me, Yahweh has led me on the way

identity_focus.core_truth: Yahweh leads me when I pray, and I can serve others with a kind heart.
identity_focus.reflection_prompt: Rebekah went above and beyond to help a stranger. What is one way you could do more than you're asked to help someone?
reflection_choices: Help clean up without being asked

micro_prayer.text: Yahweh, thank You for leading me when I pray. Give me a kind heart like Rebekah's, ready to help others even when it's hard work. Amen.

companion.message: Rebekah was my grandmother! Her kindness at that well changed our whole family's story. Small acts of kindness can be part of God's big plans.
